rationale: A coherent and correctly signed conditional reweighting of the archive's best-performing internal-funding ratio, but because the product's low tail is dominated by high-investment/deficit firms it risks collapsing onto the already-published investment and net-external-financing anomalies rather than isolating incremental funding-quality information.

Beyond being close to a direct restatement of the joint share-issuance/external-financing and capex anomalies, the funding ratio is mis-specified for cash-burning firms — with sstk=0 and oancf<0 it returns +1 (maximally "equity-dependent") despite no issuance, contaminating the short leg with pure low-profitability firms.

Same construction pathology as its equity twin (Δdltt=0 with negative oancf yields the most "debt-dependent" score without any borrowing), and what remains is largely the known net-debt-issuance plus capex anomaly pair with no new economic content.

A well-motivated and internally consistent extension of the archive's strongest accrual-versus-investment ratio, though it is an incremental denominator tweak whose informativeness is partly blunted by allowing capx−dp and aqc to offset inside the absolute value.

The construction places the large majority of firms at exactly zero (aqc≈0), so quantile sorts will be driven by ties and a thin acquirer subsample, and the surviving contrast — cash-covered versus externally funded acquirers — is close to the documented acquirer/method-of-payment underperformance literature.

Multi-year matching of cumulative cash generation to the cumulative investment program is a substantive rather than cosmetic change and is correctly signed, but stacking the horizon change with the intensity weighting simultaneously (and overlapping heavily with proposal 1) makes attribution of any improvement ambiguous.
